goal_alignment.note: plan.json covers Q1 (monthly seasonality, peak/trough, peak/trough ratio, 2023 vs 2024 replication), Q2 (weekday vs weekend hourly profile, DOW x hour heatmap, AM/PM peaks) and Q3 (member vs casual hourly, seasonal, duration) plus optional Q4 (Open-Meteo weather, explicitly time-boxed and skippable with weather_SKIPPED.md). It keeps the 3-5 finding report, cleaning counts, uncertainty (day-level bootstrap CIs, HAC errors), the association-not-causation rule, and a stop rule (DATA_UNAVAILABLE.md, no fabricated data). Caveat: the plan's proposal_id is prop_09e4bcbb, which is only the human-gate placeholder ('I think the latest proposal is fine', human_gates.jsonl gate_c9744f94, action 'propose'). The proposal the human endorsed was the 'footprint-robust atlas' (prop_e33e6001, full system vs balanced station cohort, score 5.6). The plan silently drops that cohort/footprint layer. The omission does not hurt the campaign objective, which never asked for it, but it is an unacknowledged deviation from what the human approved.

completeness.note: Five jobs (acquire-data, clean-and-aggregate, temporal-analysis, weather-association, write-report), each with parameters, expected outputs, dependencies, and checks. Cleaning rules R1-R7 are ordered, with sequential and independent counts and a sensitivity check on the <60 s rule. Row-count reconciliation, 731-date check and an anomalies note are specified. Gaps: (1) no footprint/station-cohort sensitivity job (see goal_alignment); (2) the top-level dependency_edges list is empty, although per-job 'dependencies' are filled in, so make sure the executor reads the latter; (3) R6 is worded confusingly ('outside the calendar year of its file' vs 'keep Jan 1 2023-Dec 31 2024'); the second formulation is the usable one; (4) the plan does not say how the DST fall-back duplicate hour is handled beyond mentioning it as a limitation (acceptable); (5) the plan requires findings_numbers.json to hold every quoted number but gives no schema, so traceability depends on research following through.

correctness.note: I checked the environment claims in the container (16c10c580dbd). /app is empty; pandas is not installed and curl is not installed; there are 128 CPUs and 112 GB free on the overlay, as the plan states. From Python urllib, HEAD requests to s3.amazonaws.com/tripdata gave 200 for 2023-citibike-tripdata.zip (1,602,415,356 bytes, matches the plan's 1.6 GB), 200 for 202401 (369 MB) and 202412 (451 MB), and 404 for 202301-citibike-tripdata.zip, matching the plan's claim that 2023 monthly URLs 404 and only the yearly archive exists. archive-api.open-meteo.com returned 200 for a small test query. So the data-acquisition plan is feasible and the data-availability worry raised in the ideation audit is now largely resolved. I did not verify pypi access or the exact contents of the 2023 archive (nested zips or parts), which the plan treats as an inspection step. Some size guesses (2024 monthly zips 0.4-1.0 GB, 'peak ~40 GB disk') are plausible but unverified; the 2024 Dec zip is 451 MB, within range. Methodological points are sound: the plan treats monthly totals as census counts and uses between-day bootstrap and HAC errors, avoids causal wording, and proposes a month fixed-effects sensitivity for weather. One thing to watch: the plan reads 'Hurricane/snow days are real' and flags low-count days, which is the right handling.

traceability.note: The plan fixes exact output paths (/app/output/tables/*.csv, figures/*.png, findings_numbers.json, weather_numbers.json, data_manifest.json with URLs, sizes, sha256, row counts per file) and scripts (/app/code/01-04), and requires every number in the report to come from saved tables. This gives a clear trail. Weakness: the proposal link is to a placeholder proposal, and the plan_id/proposal_id do not reflect the actual scope. The planning transcript was not read in detail; the verification above was done directly on the container and plan.json.

summary: The planning phase produced a feasible, well-specified five-job plan (acquire, clean/aggregate, temporal analysis, optional weather, report) that directly serves the campaign objective Q1-Q4, with explicit cleaning rules and counts, bootstrap/HAC uncertainty, a no-fabrication stop rule and limitations to state. I confirmed in the container that the key assumptions hold: empty /app, no pandas/curl, 128 CPUs, 112 GB free, the 2023 yearly zip and 2024 monthly zips exist on S3 (200 responses with matching sizes), 2023 monthly URLs return 404, and Open-Meteo is reachable. The main concern is that the human had approved the 'footprint-robust' proposal (balanced station cohort sensitivity) and the plan drops that layer without saying so, and it cites the placeholder proposal id prop_09e4bcbb. Because the brief itself does not require the cohort layer and the descriptive core is complete, this is passed with recommendations rather than rejected.
recommendations: Acknowledge the deviation: in the research output/report, state that the footprint (balanced station cohort) layer of prop_e33e6001 was not part of the plan, or add a small optional job after clean-and-aggregate: full system vs stations active in all 24 months (and a relaxed >=10-month cohort), comparing the seasonal shape and 2024/2023 growth. Station IDs are already in the parquet files, so this is cheap. If added, report the size of the gap, not just its sign, as the ideation audit advised.
Resolve R6 wording in 02_clean_aggregate.py: use 'started_at within 2023-01-01..2024-12-31' and also report how many trips spill across month-file boundaries.
Make sure the executor uses the per-job 'dependencies' fields (top-level dependency_edges is empty), and run in order acquire -> clean -> (temporal, weather) -> report.

In acquire-data, inspect the 2023 yearly zip listing before extracting (nested zips, multi-part CSVs, __MACOSX) and extract into fresh empty directories; read the CSVs as text, use python -I, and write data_manifest.json with sha256 and per-month row counts. If any month is missing, write DATA_UNAVAILABLE.md and continue only with the months actually obtained; do not substitute.

Verify that each of the 24 months has a plausible row count and that the member_casual and rideable_type values are as expected (e.g. 'docked_bike' only in older data) before cleaning; note the 2024 pricing/e-bike changes and the changed member_casual definition in limitations rather than as explanations.

Define the schema of findings_numbers.json up front (key -> value, CI, source table) so the report can cite every number; the final audit should be able to recompute at least peak/trough months and cleaning counts from the CSVs.

pip install duckdb/pandas/matplotlib/scipy/statsmodels/pyarrow is untested (pypi reachability was not verified by this audit); if install fails, report it and stop rather than falling back to synthetic data.
